CIRCULAR
Sub: ‘Training Calendar “Endeavour” 2009-10

The Training Calendar for the year 2009-10 of NATRSS has been finalized. The Training Calendar
has been modified from previous year’s Training Calendar keeping in view the requirements of the EPFO vis-avis BPR Project for the year based on the suggestions received from senior officers. The salient features of the
Training Calendar are as follows:

1) All the officers will have to get fully familiarized with training capsules for BPR to be able to run
the modules on their own by Sept./Oct. 2009 which is the time-frame by which all offices would
operate fully computerized modules.

2) The functional training courses would be extended to minimum 6 days till October 2009 from
present 2/3 days or 5 days course to make provision for computer training necessarily. The main
purpose of extending the programme to 6 days is that now even APFCs are entitled for Air travel
facility and may therefore stay on Saturday and thereafter get relieved on Sundays to report the
respective offices on Mondays i.e. without wastage of any working day. The second purpose is
that wherever the training programmes are of shorter duration, it would save the repeated traveling
cost and also journey time if such trainings are extended to 6 days instead of bifurcating it into two
different spells of 3 days each. In other words the short courses would be of or 2+3 days or 3+3
days.

3) For 5 days functional courses, on each of the 5 working days there would be compulsory evening
session on Computerisation with sessions on hands on computers with special reference to the
capsules designed for BPR project, which would have a trial run in Karnal on 6.4.09. On the last
day independent run exercises would be checked.

4) Keeping in view the need to improve service delivery to the subscribers and sensitise the officers
on issues relating to Customer Relationship Management one course in each quarter of the
Calendar Year has been proposed.

5) With a view to enhance the skills of officers in Performance Appraisal and Objective Reporting
and Reviewing, a 2-day workshop on ACR has been introduced.

6) Due to the increasing number of cases under the Right to Information Act 2005, a 2-day workshop
on RTI Act 2005 has been introduced.

7) Mid-career training has been introduced for RPFCs-II for 2 weeks and RPFCs-I for 2 weeks for all
the officers having completed minimum 10-15 years of service.

8) Induction courses for DP Quota APFCs have been extended to 3 weeks instead of 2 weeks. The

Induction course for DR Quota would be of 12-14 weeks if the new batch of APFCs comes. A
refresher course for APFCs has also been introduced.

9) The number of courses in the area of Recovery has been increased to 2.

10) The outbound non-functional programmes have been postponed after October 2009. However,
the additional outbound programmes could be taken earlier if functional areas are not stressed.

11) Additional capsules of computerisation programmes would be designed for the
trainers/supervisors/mentors as per BPR requirements from time to time.

The summary of NATRSS Training Calendar “Endeavour” 2009-10 is enclosed for perusal. The same
is uploaded on the NATRSS/EPFO websites www.natrss.gov.in and www.epfindia.nic.in. All officers may
be advised to take note of the above while making travel arrangements for attending the training programmes
at NATRSS.

(V.Y. SHARMA)

Sir

Your attention is invited to Head Office letter No. R-I/BPR_ Roll
Out/2008/196/68778 to 68924 dated 23.12.2008, wherein it was informed that
development of application software for the Computerization Project is in
progress in respect of the functionalities having impact on the services to the
Provident Fund members. With the technical assistance provided by NIC, an
application software has since been developed and its testing by the EPFO teams
constituted for this purpose is in progress. It has been decided to start the
parallel run in SRO, Karnal on 06.04.2009. The parallel run will continue for a
period of about 2 months and eventually the application software will be live in
SRO, Karnal on 8" June 2009.

It has also been decided to implement the computerization project in 25
fieid offices of the EPFO on 1* July 2009. List of 25 offices is annexed herewith
for your information. In rest of the offices it will be implemented w.e.f
01.10.2009.

You will appreciate that one of the important activity with regard to the
implementation of computerization project is migration of legacy data into the
new application system. The strategy for migration of legacy data into the new
system has been worked out and for cleaning of legacy data a tool viz. Data
Migration Capturing and Cleaning (DMCC) software has been developed. The

16 Rh 200

DMCC has been developed to clean the legacy data which is in soft form and also
to capture the legacy data which is in paper form and essential for roll out of the
application software. The DMCC has been successfully run in SRO, Karnal and
improved based on the feed-back received from SRO, Karnal and the same is
being forwarded through e-mail to help the field offices for determining the data
gaps and for filling up those gaps. A User Manual! for running the DMCC
software is being forwarded through e-mail.

In order to assist the field offices in creating awareness among the staff
and officers and also for the operation of DMCC software the co-ordinating
officers attached with the field offices will frequently visit the respective offices.
The co-ordinating officers will also provide clarifications to the doubts raised by
the officials of the field offices. It is also decided to train the trainers from each
office. You are therefore requested to send name of one officer & one staff
member from each office within 1 week positively. You are also requested to
give due publicity/awareness to all our staff members about the computerization
project and the time schedule mentioned hereinabove. The officer-in-charges of
the offices in list of 25 offices are requested to get in touch with the coordinating officers and ensure preparedness of their respective offices for

implementation of computerization project.

Sub:-PF Contribution on Leave Encashment — clarification

Sir,

The dispute before the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Appeal (Civil) No.
1832/2004 (Manipal Academy of Higher Educatic1. versus Provident Fund Commissioner) was
whether the amount received by encashing the earned leave is a part of “basic wage” under
section 2(b) of the Employees’ Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
requiring pro rata employer’s contribution.

Hon’ble Supreme Court of India has delivered the judgment on 12.3.2008 in the case
and concluded that the basig wage was never intended to include amounts received for leave
encashment. The appeal has been allowed by the Hon’ble Apex Court but it has also been
decided that if any payment has already been made it can be adjusted for future liabilities and
there shall not be any refund claim since the fund is running one.

In view of the Hon’ble Supreme Courts’ judgment dated 12.3.2008 in Appeal (Civil)

Subject:- Doing away with the practice of Pre-auditing of IDS of
Form 10-D /Form 10-C at Pension Section
Sir,

Based on the deliberations in the RPFC’s Conference held
during 30-31" Jan. 2009, it has been decided to do away with the practice of
Pre-auditing of the Input Data Sheet in the Pension Section with an aim to
reduce the time taken for settlement of pension cases especially in the process
of pre-auditing.

The following alternative procedure has to be followed with
immediate effect:-

1. After the approval of the Input Data Sheet (IDS) by the concerned

Sir,

This is in continuation of the Office Circular No. Wel, Fund/Women Cell/2005/20936
dated 30.5.2005 on the subject cited , a copy of which alongwith enclosures is enclosed
herewith. In accordance with the guidelines laid down by the: Supreme Court in the case of
Vishaka Vs. the State of Rajasthan and others (JT 1997 (7) ‘SC 384), certain administrative
measures are required to be implemented which are as under:

i) Constitution of a permanent Internal Complaints Committee in accordance :

with the Supreme Court guidelines. |

ti) Visible display of notice prohibiting sexual harassment in all the Offices
Prominent display of the names and contact number of the members of
the Complaints Committee.

hii) A yearly work report to be submitted to the Central Provident Fund
Commissioner from all the Regional Offices Complaints Committees as well
as Head Office complaints committee.

iv) Members of the complaints committees to be trained by the Competent
Gender Sensitive Lawyers in the procedure of handling sexual harassment
cases.

Further as the order dated 26.4.2004 passed by Supreme Court in the case of Medha ”
Kotwal Lele & Ors. Versus Union of India and Ors, the Complaint Committee referred to above

will be deemed to be an inquiry authority for the purpose of the Central Civil Services (Conduct)

Rules, 1964 and its report shall be deemed to be an inquiry report under these rules.

Since, the Complaint Committees will be deemed to be an Inquiry. Authority for the
purpose of the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964 and its report shall be deemed to be
an inquiry report under these rules, the members of the Internal Complaints Committees are

also eligible for Honorarium as per rule.

All the Regional Provident Fund Commissioners-Incharge of the Regions are requested to
constitute the Complaints Committee afresh and are requested to take apprapriate action an the

above guidelines so as to comply the guidelines of the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India.

Action on the above lines are expected to be completed: by 31.3.2009. A copy of the
action taken in this regard mav kindly be endorsed to the undersigned.

Sub: Determination of eligible service under para 9 of EPS,1995 —
Rounding off of past service and actual service

Ref:- This office circular No.Pension-A&C/1/2000/PIC/54483 dated
2.11.2001.

Sir,

On a plain reading of para 9 of EPS, 1995 it is very clear that the roundingoff of service is possible only for determining the eligibility of pension and that
too only once i.e. either rounding off of actual service for the new entrants OR
rounding off of past service for the existing members. In other words, the
rounding off of actual service is not available for existing members. Further, it
also means that the rounding-off is not available for calculating pension but
restricted only for determining the eligibility of 10 years or more. To sum up, the
facility of rounding-off of service is available under EPS-1995 only for eligible
service and that too only in the following situations:

i. Rounding-off of actual service only for new entrants for the
purpose of determining the eligible service

ii. Rounding-off of past service only for existing members for the
purpose of determining the eligible service

However, the field offices separately round-off both past service and
actual service for the purpose of determining the eligibility as stipulated vide
Para 6.2.14 of MAP Vol.III though this is not backed by the Scheme provision as
seen above. Therefore, this provision of MAP which contradicts the provisions
contained in para 9 of EPS,1995 has no force and can be considered to be

withdrawn as the Scheme provisions shall prevail over the above Manual
provisions to avoid unintended overpayments. Therefore, the rounding off of
past service or actual service has to be carried out only once for determining
the eligible service Le. only past service in respect of existing members and
only actual service in respect of new entrants and not both.

All the cases referred to Head Office in this regard can be considered
as rejected as they do not have an eligible service of 10 years or more.

Sub: Revised Estimates for the year 2008-09 - Additional budget required — Reg.
Ref: This office letter of even number dated 19.12.2008-conveying RE 2008-09.

Sir,

ft is revealed that Regional Offices of EPFO have been sending their
requisitions for allocation of additional budget to Head Office immediately after
receiving Budget Estimates/Revised Estimates under various heads in haste without
proper planning during the financial year just because tf is available or sanctioned
without considering/observing the basic financial prudence. This elucidates that
proper care was not taken at the time of submission of proposal of RE/BE. Sometimes
huge part of allotted funds is spent during the last few months. A number of
requisitions from Regional Offices have been received in this regard for allotment of
additional funds over and above budget already allotted in Revised Estimates for
2008-09.

All the Regional Offices are therefore requested to manage their expenditure
out of the budget allotted in RE 2008-09 and in case of any exigencies, a reappropriation proposal may be forwarded by 28 February 2009, strictly in the
prescribed proforma giving full justification as to why the required expenditure was
not projected in the proposal of Revised Estimates for 2008-09, duly taking into
consideration total expenditure incured as on date and anticipated expendiiure
during the current financial year. Re-appropriation proposals received from all the
Regional Offices will be consolidated and processed for approval by the CPFC, in

one go. Therefore Proposal received after 28.02.2009 will not be entertained at any

cost and any excess expenditure incurred without reappropriation/approval of Head

2

Office over and above the budget allotted under Revised Estimates would be the

sole responsibility of RPFC-I/OIC of the region.

Further, it has also been observed that Regional Offices at the first instance
surrender the projected surplus under certain budget heads at the time of sending
re-appropriation proposal and gets the shown surplus re-appropriated to another
budget head. But later on, after the end of the financial year, another proposal is
sent to ratify the excess expenditure incurred in that particular (same) budget head
in which savings were offered in re-appropriation proposal. It shows the wrong
projection of the saving at the time of re-appropriation, which finally leads to excess
expenditure. It should be kept in mind while forwarding the proposal for reappropriation to Headquarters that such wrong projection does not occur.

Before sending the requisition to Head Office, following points should be kept
in mind: -

1) — Allotment of budget in RE 2008-09 under the head ‘Dearness Pay’ has been
made based on the expenditure incured upto 31.08.2008 only so as to
regularize the said expenditure. Further, after implementation of the 6th
Central Pay Commission, expenditure for the purpose of ‘Grade Pay’ is
included under the head ‘Pay of Officers’ and ‘Pay of Establishments’ and
budget in RE 2008-09 has been allotted accordingly.

2) Incase, some special sanction has been accorded by the RPFC-I/Addl. CPFC
for_any unforeseen expenditure, in that case also, first of all availability of
budget as allotted in BE/RE should be taken into account and in case of
insufficient/no budget available under that particular budget head, then only
matter should be referred to Headquarters for additional allocation.

3) Allotment/additional allotment of funds for special budget heads viz.
‘Computerisation’, ’Staff Welfare Fund’, ‘Purchase of Motor Vehicles’ and
‘Capital Expenditure’ may be forwarded directly to their respective Divisional
Heads in Head Office instead of sending it to the Budget Section as total
budget under these heads is kept under their disposal.

4) In case of non-recuring/unusual kind of expenditure i.e. opening of new
offices, visit of parliamentary committees etc., requisition should accompany
the copy of administrative approval by Competent Authority to incur such
expenditure in the absence of which proposal would not be entertained in

Headauarters.

Subject: Filing of Special Leave Petitions before the Hon’ble Supreme
Court of India.

or As you must be aware, filing of appeals before the Hon’ble Supreme
Court of India has to be undertaken in a time bound manner. In order to ensure that
the appeals don’t become time barred, it is essential that all the relevant documents are
available with the Legal Cell in time.

2. The following documents are absolutely essential for filing an appeal
before the Hon’ble Supreme Court and as such any proposal for filing of an SLP must be
accompanied with them -

Attention is invited to various complaints received from PF members and other
stakeholders of EPFO in the matter of delay and harassment caused to our clients in regulating
and providing the statutory services in the prescribed time limits. The complaints also point out
the irregular practices being adopted in some field offices by causing abnormal delays in
proViding the reasonable benefit related services and demand and acceptance of illegal
gratification. Needless to say, the said unfair practices will not only bring down the service
standards of the organization but also expose the indiscriminate exercise of the powers vested
on the concerned officials and shows the orqanlzation in a poor light despite the hardwork and
promptness exhibited by the major chunk of officials.
2.
On an analysis of the complaints, the irregular practices are observed broadly in the
followlnq work areas:
i. Harassment and delay caused in settlement of benefit claims to the members.
ii. Coverage of establishments and initiating compliance related quasi-judicial actions in
determination of dues and recovery thereof.
iii. Anowing the representatives of the employers to be associated with the official work of
EPFO.
iv. Appearance of Persons in the guise of authorized representative other than the officials
of the establishments in the quasi-judicial proceedings.
v. Misusing the official data regarding claim processing details by the insiders in
connivance with outsiders and misguiding the customers for ulterior motves.
3.
In one case of delay in settlement of advance claim, based on the complaint received
from the PF member, OIC has caused investigations through EPFO. Based on the investigation
details, and its analysis in depth, OIC has observed as under:
"EPFO is allowing the representatives ofemployers to be associated with the official work of
the EPFO. The Commission has further observed that if this undesirable practice continues,

the EPFO officials shall be liable for the misconduct ofoutsiders who are alleged to be used
as conduits for demand and acceptance of J1Iegal gratification. The Commission would
therefore advise the EPFO to stop immediately the practice oftaking assistance ofoutsiders
for the official work ofthe organization. II
4.
The above advice of the evc should be followed and implemented in letter and spirit.
There should be no deviation from the official process of working as per norms, procedures and
manual of accounting instructions etc. Any deviation in this regard will attract the disciplinary
actions against the concerned officials. "It is the responsibility of the Supervisory and
Administrative Authorities to exercise due control and authority in the respective field offices
and take preventive steps to identify such irregular practices and take effective action.
5.
In order to curtail the glaring instances of such unfair practices, I would like to make it
clear that all the OICs and other officers should conduct preventive vigilance exercise in their
respective field offices as a supportive arrangement to elimin,ate malpractices, if any.
6.
Please acknowledge receipt of this circular and intimate the action taken in this regard.

Sir,

Attention is invited to GOI Notifications G.S.R. 705(E) & 706(E) DATED 1°"
October 2008 amending the EPS, 1995 and EPFS, 1952 to make special provisions
for the International workers.

The salient features of the scheme are as under:

1. It covers also an International worker as defined under Para 2 ff of the
scheme for whom the EPF & MP Act, 1952 applies and who are mobile
internationally.

2. Subject to the exclusion provision, this class of employees (International
workers) covers certain category of Indian employees (holding Indian
passport) and all the employees holding other than an Indian passport.

3. International workers and their employers have to contribute on the full salary
without any ceiling.

4. Every eligible international worker shall be enrolled with effect from 1°
November 2008 (the beginning of the month following that in which the
scheme came into force).

5. The payment of benefits in respect of employees holding other than Indian
passport hailing from the countries with which India has signed a Social
Security Agreement (SSA) shall be governed, wherever applicable, by the
provisions of the SSA. (Although, as of now India has signed SSA with
Belgium, France and Germany, the date of effect is yet to be notified.
Therefore, as of now, all the eligible employees holding passport other
than Indian passport and working in an_ establishment
covered/coverable under the Act, shall be required to be enrolled while
no Indian employee is entitled to become an International worker).

the countries with which India has NOT signed a SSA the payment of

Subject: - Strengthening & streamlining of public grievances handling mechanism - focused
publicity to create awareness among our customers and resolving grievances.
Sir,
1. Your attention is drawn to the instructions issued on the above subject by the
Headquarters from time to time to expedite the process of resolving grievances.

2. On a quick review of the issues connected to the customer services, it is felt
necessary to impress upon you the need and the necessity to streamline the
handling of public grievances. In this context, the following requirements are
highlighted to publicize and create awareness for the members to understand the
services provided by EPFO for availing hassle-free services for resolving their
benefit related grievances -

I. All the officers-in-charge of field offices shall open their e-mails on day to
day basis and take necessary action to provide the replies through e-mail to
the members within 7-10 working days.

Il. Bhavishya Nidhi Adalats are being organized by all the field offices on 10"
of every month or on the next working day, if 10" happens to be a public
holiday. This needs to be publicized every month well in advance through
print and electronic media for the information of the members. Besides,

you may apprise the Labour Secretary/ Labour Commissioner of the state /
area so that they would be in a position to create awareness amongst the
workers / trade unions for attending the Bhavishya Nidhi Adalats to
represent their grievances.

I. To begin with, Bhavishya Nidhi Adalats for the month of January, 2009
may be organized on 10'"/ 12" as the case may be, immediately. Please
be in touch with the Labour Secretary/ Labour Commissioner and seek
their cooperation for the purpose mentioned above. The result of the
Adalats be informed by 13'" to the Headquarters.

IV. Every month the Bhavishya Nidhi Adalats are to be activated and
regulated with due publicity and awareness and the progress be reported
by 15" of every month.

V. All the officers-in-charge of field offices shall indicate the timings for
meeting the members whose grievances are not resolved. This should be
carried out on all the working days at a specified time.

VI. All the claims received as on 31" December 2008 shall be finalized and
settled by 31° of January 2009. Every month 3 oldest pending claim
cases be taken up for scrutiny by the officer-in-charge and quick action
to finalize the same be taken. Also report the status in the monthly MIS
returns to be sent to the Headquarters.

VU. The grievances recorded in CPGRAMS need to be attended on a day to
day basis by the officers-in-charge and post the replies in a proper
manner regularly. No case should remain without furnishing the replies
in 7-10 working days.

VIII. ‘Know Your Claim Status” facility provided in the central website be
uploaded on 10", 20", 30" of every month duly forwarding the updated
data to NDC by all the field offices. Any laxity in this regard will be
viewed seriously.

IX. Public Relation Officers in the cadre of AAOs shall be made available in
the Facilitation Centers of all the field offices with the required
supporting staff and the system arrangements.

X. In all the field offices, the customers are to be attended in a proper and
courteous manner and all the phone calls received therein are to be
attended to without any laxity.

Sub: Instructions for strict following of the provisions of Manual of Accounting Procedure
in the maintenance of Valuable Documents Register in sending the cheques received
for collection and for advising the employers to remit the dues in the Bank only through
the prescribed Challans.

It has been brought to the notice of the undersigned, during a Meeting with the State Bank
of India on 24-11-2008 that a sizable number of cheques received through VDR (Valuable
Documents Register) are sent for realisation to the Bank after the lapse of 3 to 4 months. As such,

this is a serious lapse so far as Interest Loss is concerned.

2. Instructions contained in Chapter 7, Para 7.8.1 to 7.8.6 of the Manual of Accounting
Procedure, Part ~ I, General clearly stipulates that the cheques received from the employers directly
in the office are required to be entered in the VDR and after preparing the Challans, they should be
sent to Bank for realisation on the same day of their receipt or the following day and no cheque
should be detained for more than 02 days. Besides, the employers are required to be advised to
remit the amounts in the nearest branch of the State Bank only and to submit the Challans to the

office.

3. Contrary to these instructions, cheques are indiscriminately being received from the
employers and being submitted to the Bank for realisation after a long delay. The Audits have also

been highlighting this serious lapse, time and again, in their reports.

YOR Cir R*

4.- In view of this your immediate attention is drawn to the instructions contained in the
Manual of Accounting Procedure, as stated above, for strict adherence. Further, the employers be
addressed immediately to remit the dues directly to the Bank and to forward the Challans only.
For any laxity in this regard the RC (F&A) / OIC would personally be held responsible for the

loss caused to the Funds.

5. OICs are requested to review the above position to send a compliance report by 30°
December 2008 for one, that there are no pending cheques under VDRs for presentation to the
Bank, two, Manual provisions are being strictly observed and three the employers have adequately
been addressed for direct remittance to the Bank..

(This issues with the approval of Central Provident Fund Commissioner)

Sub: Enrolment of workers engaged in Building & Construction Industries.

Sir,

As you are aware the establishments engaged in Building and Construction was brought
under the purview of the Act w.e.f. 31% October, 1980. As per statistics available there are more
than 8 million workers engaged in B&C Industries throughout the country. As on March, 2008,
the number of establishments covered under Building & Construction is 13409 and the
members enrolled is 9,56,900, which is nowhere near the actual workforce employed in B&C
Industry.

In order to identify the establishments, the provisions contained in the Building and Other
Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 which
came into force w.e.f. 19" August, 1996, may be utilized for collecting the details including the
names of the workers employed in the industry. On perusal of the above Act, the relevant
sections relating to identification of employers and workers, issue of ID card and maintenance of
registers and records are reproduced below :-

Section 7 Registration of establishments:- (1) Every employer shall, -

(a) in relation to an establishment to which this Act applies on its commencement,
within a period of sixty days from such commencement; and
(b) in relation to any other establishment to which this Act may be applicable at any

time after such commencement, within a period of sixty days from the date on
which this Act become applicable to such establishment.

Make an application to the registering officer for the registration of such establishment.

Section 12 Registration of building workers as beneficiaries — (1) every building worker
who has completed eighteen years of age, but has not completed sixty years of age, and who
has been engaged in any building or other construction work for not less than ninety days during
the preceding twelve months shall be eligible for registration as a beneficiary under this Act.

Section 13 Identity Cards: - (1) The Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare
Board shail give to every beneficiary an identity card with his photograph duly affixed thereon
and with enough space for entering the details of the building or other construction work done
by him.

Section 30 Maintenance of registers and records — (1) Every employer shall maintain
such registers and records giving such particulars of building workers employed by him, the
work performed by them, the number of hours of work which shall constitute a normal working

Fage 1% 3

day for them, a day of rest in each period of seven days which shail be allowed to them, the
wages paid to them, the receipts given to them and such other particulars in such form as may
be prescribed.

Also vide Section 4 of the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of
Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996, a State Advisory Committee is required to be
constituted by the State Government to advise on such matters arising out of the administration
of this Act. The members of the Committee inter-alia consists of the Chief Inspector of the
Factories as Ex-Officio Member.

In addition to the above, according to the Building and Other Construction Workers’
Welfare Cess Act, 1996 wherein as per Rule 7, the employer is required to submit information
in Form 1 which inter-alia contain details of commencement of work, number of workers
employed etc. A copy of Form | is enclosed for information.

Sub: Handling of complaints received on Compliance related matters- detailed
procedure to be followed — reg.
Sir,

References are being received in the Head Office from various Central Trade Unions

and individuals that their complaints relating to compliance related issues are not properly
handled in the field offices.

2.

There has been number of references also to Head Office requesting to formulate a

uniform procedure to be followed in respect of such complaints. The matter has since been
examined and the following guidelines are issued for uniform compliance by ail the Regions.

First Category

In many cases the complaints are received through anonymous letters. While
normaily no cognizance is taken in respect of such anonymous complaints, if such
anonymous complaints contains verifiable facts, such anonymous complaints can be
acted upon by deputing an EO to the establishment mentioned in the complaint for
causing a detailed inquiry in the matter.

Second

Sometimes the complaints are received from individuals without mentioning any
details or enclosing any documentary evidence. In such cases reference has to be
made to the complainant to furnish whatever information/documentary evidences in
his/her possession for initiating action. Only after receipt of such
information/evidence further action need be taken in respect of such complaints to
its logical end.

Third Category

Complaints are also received from Trade Unions giving a general information
regarding evasion in membership/non coverage of establishments. In such cases a
reference has to be made to such Trade Unions to furnish documentary evidence if
any in their possession substantiating the evasion and also the details of the
establishments which have not been covered. After receipt of such information

further inquiry can be initiated in respect of such complaints for causing inspection/
action for enrollment/ coverage as the case may be.

° Fourth Category

In respect of complaints received from Trade Unions giving specific information
regarding evasion in membership, inquiry under Para 26B has to be first initiated
to determine the eligibility of the member. The employer, the concerned employees
and the complainant Trade Unions need to be called for the inquiry before deciding
the issue.

After deciding the eligibility for enrollment of the employee inquiry u/s 7A has to be
initiated for assessment of the dues payable in respect of such members. At the
time of inquiry under @ection 7A the complainant may be called for the inquiry if
required depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case.

e Fifth Category

Many references are being received from PMO, Ministry of Labour and Member of
Parliament/Assembly and CBT Members etc. (VIP References) regarding matters
relating to non-enrollment/non-coverage of establishments. In such cases the EO
need to be deputed immediately to the concemed establishment/area and a detailed
report need to be obtained without making any back references.

The various complaints which are generally received have been categorized under
the five heads above. There may be other complaints which does not fall under the above
five categories. All OICs are requested to deal with all such cases on the lines broadly
indicated above which are only illustrative and not exhaustive.

It should be ensured that all references received are acted upon with due diligence
and urgency and prompt reply sent to the complainants and to Head Office where the cases
are referred for investigation and report.

(This issues with the approval of Central PF Commissioner)

Yours faithfully,
( P. SUDHA U)

Obsolescence Policy for Computer Hardware & Peripherals
[Approved by the Central Board of Trustees’, EPF in its 183 meeting held on 05.07.08]

With almost two decades since the deployment of computer infrastructure
commenced in the organization, a pressing need has been felt to address the problem
of functional and technical obsolescence of the computer hardware and peripherals.

Since there is a large degree of dependence on computer applications for the
smooth functioning and operation of the offices of the Organization, an obsolescence
policy has been devised for computer hardware and peripherals to streamline the
process of replacement of old and obsolete systems and peripherals. The obsolescence
policy has been approved by CBT, EPF in its 183 meeting held on 05.07.08.

The obsolescence policy as devised has cycle times defined in a manner that IT
infrastructure items are retained long enough to get full use out of them and are
decommissioned at appropriate time to ensure smooth operations. It is emphasized
that while the obsolescence policy prescribes a recommended productive /
economic lifetime for equipment it does not propose a compulsory
decommissioning of systems after this period. The decision for earmarking systems
as obsolete has to be a considered decision taken on the basis of prescribed criteria
and the systems would continue to be utilized to the extent possible and practicable.

The under mentioned Obsolescence policy as approved by the Central Board of
Trustees’, EPF has been adopted for use in the Organisation:

(A\. Eauinment whose individual cost is in excess of Rs 10 lakhs: These being
expensive equipment should be generally placed under support with the Original
Equipment Manufacturers (OEM). The Obsolescence of such equipment will be
decided in consultation with the OEM and the determination should take into
account the end of life and end of support notifications of the OEM, the
equipments’ integration compatibility with other equipment that is present or
newly acquired for specific needs of EPFO and other technical considerations
that may be relevant for such determination. However, this period should not
normally be less than 8 years.

(B). For items / equipments whose individual cost was less than Rs. 10 lakh:
The productive lifetime should be uniformly five (05) years including the warranty
period.

(a) After the end of the five (05) years lifetime, these equipment can continue
to be used to the extent possible. A judicious decision needs to be taken
on its continuing maintenance & upkeep after this period.

(b) Beyond the prescribed lifetime i.e. productive / economic lifetime of five
(05) years, obsolescence may be determined based on the foliowing
criteriaa. Physical condition

Sub: Revision of Pay scales of Officers and employees of EPFO — adoption
of resolution No.1/1/2008-IC dated 29.08.2008, Revised CCS (Pay)
Rules, 2008 by the CBT — Regarding.

Sir,

Please refer to this office letter No.HRD/1(2)/2008/6" CPC/34632-682
dated 09.09.2008.

2. The Central Board of Trustees in its Special Meeting held on
18.09.2008 has adopted the Resolution No. 1/1/2008-IC dated 29.08.2008
Issued by the Government of India accepting the recommendations of the 6”
CPC for applying to its officers and employees The Board has also adopted
the CCS Revised Pay Rules, 2008 for applying the revised scales of pay of
officers and employees of the EPFO. Consequent on the adoption of the
above orders, supra, the revised pay scales has become applicable to the
officers and employees of the organization. The copies of the Resolution and
CCS (Revision of Pay) Rules, 2008 etc is available in the website

http-//india.gov.in/govi/ipaycommission.php , a copy each of which may be
taken by the individual offices.

3. Consequent on the adoption of pay scales the implementation of
revised pay scales need to be done by following the instructions contained in
O.M No.1/1/2008-IC dated 30.08.2008 of Ministry of Finance a copy of which
is available on the above website. The following steps shall therefore to be
taken to revise the pay scales of the officers and employees of the
organization:

i} A) the option from all the officers and employees shall be got exercised
for electing the date on which the revised pay scale are opted,

B) to obtain an undertaking from all the officers and employees that any
excess payment detected in the light of discrepancies noted
subsequently will be refunded by him or same will be adjusted
against future payments due to him.

il) Once the option is received the fixation of pay in the revised pay

band shall be done in accordance with the directions contained in
O.M No.1/1/2008-IC dated 30.08.2008.

iil) The DA shall be drawn as per the instructions contained in
memorandum No. 1(3)/2008-E-I|(B) dated 29.08.2008.

iv) HRA shall be drawn as per the instructions contained in
memorandum No.2(3)/2008-E-II(B) dated 29.08.2008.

a) Transport Allowance shall be drawn as per the instructions
contained in memorandum No.21(2)/2008-E-||(B) dated 29.08.2008.

vi) As regards to the fixation of pay in respect of Sr.SSA, Section
Supervisor and EO/AAO in the revised pay band, the fixation in the
revised pay band shall be done by applying the grade pay of
Rs.4200/- initially. The proposal for upgrading the grade pay of
EO/AAO to Rs.4600/- as applicable to the corresponding to the
scale of pay Rs.7450-11500, could be implemented only after few
technical issues are resolved for which a separate communication
will follow. Until such time all the above three grades shall draw the
revised pay in the pay band Rs.9300-34800 with grade pay of
Rs.4200/-.

vii) 40% of the arrears payable shall be paid before the Puja festival.
As per the instructions contained in O.M dated 30.08.2008 the
arrears of Ist instalment be released without following the
requirement of pre-audit and subject to adjustment of excess
payment , if any from the pay and allowances of the next months /
arrears payable in 2009-10. The Bill be post audited after releasing
the arrears.

4 Consequent on the adoption of pay scales and the acceptance of the
recommendations of the 6" CPC the orders relating to the conditions of
service relating to pay and allowances, children education assistance,
reimbursement of tuition fee allowance for physically handicapped children,
maternity leave, child care leave, etc shall also be automatically applied to the
officers and employees of the EPFO.

5. The Board has also adopted the decision of the central government in
resolution No.38/37/08-P&PW (a) dated 29.08.2008 (copy available on the
aforesaid website) accepting the recommendations of the 6" CPC relating to

Sir,

Reference is invited to Headquarters letter No. WSU-28 (1) 2003/delegation dated
13.04.2004 on the revised delegation of financial powers. It has been decided by Central
Provident Fund Commissioner to further delegate the powers under the budget head
“Computerisation” to other officers as per annexure ‘A’ under powers of delegation
available under Para 24(3) of the EPF Scheme, 1952. The delegated powers are to be
exercised by officers to whom powers have been delegated in consultation with the
officers as mentioned in Annexure ‘A’.

2. Reference is also invited to Headquarters letter No IS-3 (2) 2003/Budget
Delegation dated 01.04.2004 wherein the items of computer equipments, peripherals and
consumables have been specified for purchase by Regional Provident Fund
Commissioners (Grade-{), In-charge of Regions under budget head “Computerisation”.
Considering the revised delegation of powers and the technology changes that have since
taken place, it has been decided to revise the list of items. The revised list of items along
with limitations for each item has been mentioned in Annexure ‘B’. This is in super
cession of earlier instructions in this regard.

3. Following general guidelines are to be followed while using the delegated
powers: -

(a) Officers who have been delegated powers under “Computerisation” must
satisfy themselves in consultation with the appropriate officials (as per

Subject: Policy decision on use of Thin Clients in place of Dumb Terminals in the
field offices of the Organisation-Regarding.

Sir,

This office has been receiving several requests from various field offices for
providing Thin Clients in lieu of Dumb Terminals. They have been expressing difficulty
in procuring Dumb Terminals in some places as these had become obsolete. The issue
has been examined at Headquarters and the Competent Authority has approved the use of
Thin Clients in place of Dumb Terminals in offices of Organisation to meet the present
requirements and Project related requirements in future.

2. In the first instance, the Thin Clients can be utilized under Unix environment in
lieu of Dumb Terminals. Later the same can be utilized in relation to the “ Re-inventing
EPF, India “ Project.

a The minimum configuration of Thin Client that are deemed to meet the present
and future requirements of EPFO are as under:-

Thin clients 1 GHZ or above under Windows XP with LE browser having 512
MBRAM. 512 MB IDE Flash Memory, USB Keyboard, 2 Button Scroll Mouse, Local and

Networking Printer Support, Network Port, TCP/IP and PPP support Protocols, 4 USB
Ports, | Parallel, 1 Serial, 1 RJ-45, 1 VGA and I PS/2 Port, Windows XP Service Pack 2
LE 6.0 or above browser, Enterprise Client Management Software, Emulation Suite
DHCP FTP enabled Flash upgrade, VNC Server and Tx. Multi_User/Single User

Logan support locally.

4. It is, therefore, advised that thin clients may be purchased in lieu of dumb
terminals after making a prudent and justifiable assessment of requirements for the
currently running applications on Foxbase+ under Unix Environments. Such
assessments should not include any projected requirements under the BPR Project.
Existing working dumb terminals should remain in use and should not be replaced.

Sub:- Incentives to employers in the private sector for providing regular
employment to the persons with disabilities- regarding.

Sir,

To promote employment of persons with disabilities in the private sector, the
Central Government has approved an incentive scheme to employers in the private

sector for providing employment to the persons with disabilities (Copy of the mcentive

scheme is enclosed).

Under the scheme, the employees with disabilities covered under the persons
with disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act,
1995 and the National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy,
Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999 and working m the private
sector, with monthly wage upto Rs.25,000/- per month would be covered. The scheme
would be applicable to all the employers of employees with disabilities, who are

appointed on or after 01.4.2008.

The employer shall be given incentive to give employment to persons with
disabilities. Incentive shall be in the form of payment by Government of the employer’s

contribution to the Employees Provident Fund and Employees State Insuramce for the

first three years. The administrative charges of 1.1% of the wages of employees
covered under the Employees’ Provident Fund & Miscellaneous Provisions Act. 1952

will continue to be paid by the employer.

In order to implement the incentive scheme, the Central Govemmment has
incorporated enabling provisions in the Employees Provident Fund Scheme, 1952 by
inserting paragraph 82 vide Ministry of Labour and Employment Notification No. G. S.
R. 253 (E) published in the Gazette of India Extraordinary dated 31.3.2008. Similar
provision have also been inserted in paragraph 4 and paragraph 24 of the Employees”
Pension Scheme 95 vide Ministry of Labour and Employment Notification No. G.S.R.
252 (E) dated 31.3.2008 (Copy of both the Notifications are enclosed).

The incentive scheme as approved by the Central Government has mow to be _
implemented in right earmest by all the field offices of Employees’ Provident Fund

Organization and the following directions are issued for compliance:

1) The incentive scheme be brought to the notice of all concerned inctuding the
State Chambers of Commerce & Industry, District Industry Centres, Employment
Exchanges, Special Employment Exchanges, Vocational Training Centres etc. so that

persons with all types of disabilities get opportunity for employment in the private
sector.

il) The employers would be allowed to avail benefit under the incentive scteme on
submitting the details of employees in the form specially prescribed for the purpose
(Copy enclosed) alongwith a copy of the disability certificate (standard fonmats of the
certificate prescribed by Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment enclosed) issued
to the disabled employee by the Competent Authority under the Persons with
Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995
and the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full
Participation) Rules, 1996, (copy indicating the definition of disability under the

relevant Acts enclosed) first time when such benefits are claimed.

must not be assigned to all functional wings.

AWARE OF THE NEED TO MAINTAIN STRICT CONFIDENTIALLY AND
SECRECY OF THEIR OWN PASSWORDS.

Subject: - Break in service- clarification-regarding.
Sir/Madam
On the issue of clarification on regularization of break in
service. a circular was issued vide this office letter No. Pension
5(16)2001/TN/22385 dated 8-6-2005. Thereafter several references
were received from the field offices seeking further clarifications. Hence,
it is thought fit to revisit the issue and the following guidelines are
communicated for further course of action.
As per para 2.(xii) of EP$'95
"Past service" means the period of service rendered by an
existing member from the date of joining Employees' Family Pension
Fund till the 15th November, 1995.
As per para 9(bl of EP$'95
In the case of the"existing member" the aggregate of actual
service and the 'past service' shall be treated as eligible service.
Provided that if there is any period in the "past service" for which the
contributions towards the Family Pension Scheme, 1971 has not been
received, the said period shall count as eligible service only if the
contributions thereof have been received in the Employees' Pension
Fund.
Explanation - - for the purpose of this sub-paragraph the total past
service for less than six months shall be ignored and the total past
service for six months and above shall be rounded to a year.
Contd....2.

.2.
Hence from the above prOVISions it is very clear that only past
service for which the contributions have been received, shall be counted
for arriving at the eligible service. In other words, the breaks, if ,any,
irrespective of the period even not regularized, have to be necessarily
subtracted from the past service to arrive at the eligible service.. Thus
it is needless to say that any break - in - service exceeding one year
prior to 1.4.88 will not result in any cessation of membership as such,
but would only be liable to be
subtracted from the total past service
along with other breaks if any, for
arriving at the eligibility for pension
as well as calculating the pensionary benefits.

NOTIFICATION

G.S.R._____________ In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 6A, read with subsection (1) of section 7 of the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions
Act, 1952), (19 of 1952), the Central Government hereby makes the following Scheme
further to amend the Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995, namely:-

1. (1) This Scheme may be called the Employees’ Pension (Amendment)
Scheme, 2006.

(2) It shall come into force on the date of its publication in the Official
Gazette.

2. In the Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995:-

(a)
in paragraph 27, for sub-paragraph (2):- the following sub-paragraph
shall be substituted, namely :-

“(2) All administrative expenses shall be met from the ‘Central
Administration Account’ as specified in paragraph 49 of the
Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952. However, the cost of
remittance of Pension shall be charged on the Pension Fund”.

PENSION CALCULATION MADE EASY

Calculation of Member Pension

• Pension is calculated separately for Past Service & Pensionable Service

Procedure for Calculation of Past Service Pension

¾ Find out the total past service ie. Subtract the Date of Joining (if it is before
15.11.1995) from 15.11.1995 duly rounding the service in years
¾ Find out the salary as on 15.11.1995 as to whether it is upto Rs.2500 or more than
Rs.2500
¾ Accordingly locate the past service benefit from the table given in 12(3)(b)
¾ Find out the period that had elapsed between 16.11.1995 and the date of exit and
based on this period locate the corresponding Table ‘B’ Factor
Date of Exit is

Date of attaining 58 years for superannuation/early pension

Date of Death for widow pension

Date of Disablement for Disablement pension
¾ Multiply the Past Service Benefit and the Table ‘B’ factor which gives the Past
Service Pension

Procedure for calculation of Pensionable Service Pension

¾ Find out the Category of the member as to whether he belongs to X, Y or Z Category
X – Date of commencement of pension is between 16.11.1995
and 15.11.2000
Y – Date of commencement of pension is between 16.11.2000
and 15.11.2005
Z – Date of commencement of pension on or after 16.11.2005

¾ Find out the Pensionable Service and Pensionable Salary of the member and
substitute the same in the formula given in para 12(2)
¾ If the formula pension calculated is less than 335/438/635 respectively for X,Y,Z
categories then only that minimum pension is to be given

Procedure for calculation of Total Aggregate Pension

¾ Add the Past Service Pension and the Formula Pension
¾ If the total pension is less than 500/600/800 respectively for X,Y,Z categories than
that minimum pension shall be the total pension
¾ But this total pension is for an eligible service of 24 years or more, and if the eligible
service is less than 24 years, then this total pension has to be proportionately reduced
subject to a minimum of 265/325/450 depending on X,Y,Z categories (only when the
minimum pension is given)
¾ If the total pension itself is more than the minimum then the proportionate reduction
need not be made even if the eligible service is less than 24 years

The above calculation is only for existing members. For new entrants the pension is strictly as
per the formula given in 12(2) without applying any minimum

Calculation of Widow Pension
• If the member dies in service then
•
Widow Pension = Member Pension treating the date of death as date of retirement
(or) Table ‘C’ factor (or) Rs.450, whichever is higher
• If the member dies away from service before 58
•
With total service more than 10 years then
¾ Widow Pension = Member Pension treating the date of exit as date of
retirement (or) Table ‘C’ factor (or) Rs.450, whichever is higher
•
With total service less than 10 years
¾ And member is not a bachelor then
•
Widow Pension = Table ‘C’ factor
¾ And member is a bachelor then
•
No Pension Payable but a lumpsum amount equal to ROC payable to
nominee or parent
• If the member dies as a pensioner
•
Widow Pension = 50% of the Member Pension (or) Rs.450, whichever is higher


Calculation of Children Pension
• 25% of the widow pension calculated as above or Rs.150/- whichever is higher is payable to
every child upto 25 years starting from the death of the member

Calculation of Orphan Pension
• 75% of the widow pension calculated as above or Rs.250/- whichever is higher, is payable to
every child upto 25 years starting from the death of the widow/widower

Calculation of Withdrawal Benefit

Withdrawal Benefit is calculated separately for past service and pensionable service and then
aggregated.
Withdrawal Benefit for Past Service = Wages as on 15.11.1995 X Corresponding Table ‘A’
factor for the past service rendered X Table ‘B’ factor for the period between 16.11.1995 to the date
of exit from employment or date of attaining 58 years whichever is earlier

Withdrawal Benefit for Pensionable Service = Wages as on date of exit X Corresponding Table
‘D’ factor

Attention is invited to the following circulars:-

1. Circular No.Pen/4(2)96/SLP/Vol.V/16598 dated 26.6.2004.
2. Letter No. Pen.4 (38).96/WB/59867 dated 1.12.2004.
3. Circular No.Pen/Misc/2006/Vol.I dated 25.4.2006.


Instructions have already been issued by this office on the issue of contributing
on a pay exceeding the statutory limit under Para 11(3) of the Employees’ Pension
Scheme, 1995. However, the field offices are finding it difficult to take decisions. As a
result this office has been receiving a number of references from field offices, not to
speak of the volley of grievances being aired by the members through various channels.
Therefore it has become necessary for this office to issue guidelines in a more clear term.


While deciding the issue the following provisions may be kept in mind:

1) Under EPS there is no contribution payable separately. Under Para 3 of the
EPS, from and out of the contributions payable by the employer in each month
under Section 6 of the Act, the employer shall remit a part of contribution
representing 8.33 percent of the Employees pay to the EPS. Therefore, it is
only the employer’s share of contribution payable under Employees Provident
Fund Scheme, 1952 that is being diverted to EPS to the extent as aforesaid.
2) Accordingly, the option to contribute on a pay exceeding statutory limit is
available to a member only under Para 26(6) of the Employees Provident
Fund Scheme, 1952 and not under Para 11(3) of the EPS.
3) In fact Para 11(3) clarifies the methodology of determination of pensionable
salary only.

2
4) Since opting to contribute on higher pay to EPS means a contribution on
higher pay to Provident Fund as well, Para 11(3) provision will apply to only
such of those employees who have been contributing on a higher pay under
Para 26(6) of the Employees Provident Fund Scheme, 1952.
Accordingly the grievances may be classified into the following categories and
the issues be decided.


1. In all such cases where the employee has contributed over and above the
statutory limit either from 16.3.1996 or from the month in which his salary
exceeded the limit after having exercised his option and the same having been
accepted by the Office, the pensionable salary will be based on such salary.

2. If the option was not exercised at the time of salary crossing the statutory limit
or on 16.3.1996, as the case may be and the contribution was deposited on
salary exceeding the limit after receiving instructions from the Office before
the date of issue of circular dated 22.6.2004, the department has the vicarious
liability (restricted to the specific case only) of honouring such a commitment
and hence the pensionable salary shall be on the actual salary i.e. on the salary
(exceeding the statutory limit) on which the contribution was paid. However,
this is subject to i) a satisfactory explanation to be obtained and taken on
record from the officer who made such a commitment. ii) the employer having
remitted the administration charges and other contributions on such higher
salary.

3. In the cases where no option was given or no commitment was made by the
concerned Office, but the contribution on higher pay was deposited by the
establishment/ employee, on their own such excess contributions will be
considered as erroneous contributions and the pensionable salary will be
restricted to the statutory ceiling existing from time to time.

So all field offices are requested to consider the grievances voiced under Para
11(3) in accordance with the above clarification and decide the issues at their level
without referring them to the Head Office unnecessarily.

(This issues with the approval of CPFC)


Yours faithfully,

Sub:- Change of date of birth of Employees’ Pension Fund member- regarding

Sir,


A firm date of birth is an extremely relevant component in determination of
benefits under the EPS, 1995. Several correspondences are being received from
stakeholders as well as the field offices seeking the intervention of Head Office whenever
there is a disagreement on the date of birth. Although a number of circulars have been
issued, the problems still persist. Therefore, it has become necessary to issue
comprehensive guideline to find a workable solution to this vital issue.


Accordingly in supersession of all the earlier directions issued on the subject, the
following comprehensive guidelines are issued with immediate effect:-

i)
In cases where a member, who has not been issued with a social security
number, disputes the date of birth at the time of exit the instructions as
contained in Annexure - I may be followed.
ii)
In cases where a member, who has been issued with a social security
number, disputes the date of birth the same cannot be entertained unless
supported by a valid documentary proof such as:

• Certificate issued by the Registrar of Births and Deaths.
• Any school/education related certificate.
• Certificate based on the service records of the Central/State Government
organisation.
• Passport.

2
• In the absence of proof of age/DOB as above, Medical Certificate issued
by competent Civil Surgeon after examining the member medically and
supported with an affidavit on oath by the member duly authenticated by
Competent Court.

iii)
In cases of Social Security Number registration in which members are
required to give date of birth, our office need not to verify the same with our
records.
iv)
The disputes may be resolved at the level of officers in charge of Pension
wing of Regional/Sub-Regional offices in order to ensure a trouble free
service to the members.

(This issues with the approval of CPFC)

Subject: Exemption under Section 17(1)(a) of the EPF & MP Act,
1952 and under para 274A of the EPF Scheme, 1952.

Sir,

i; You are aware that consequent to the significant legislative

development by way of Clause 56, Finance Act, 2006, considerable emphasis has
been laid on the disposal of applications for exemption under Section 17 of. the
EPF & MP Act, 1952. In this context, it is important to realize that the
applications for exemption are addressed to the appropriate government and
hence all complete applications must be placed before the same for a final
decision. Incomplete applications must hence be returned to the applicant

employer with an exhaustive list of missing documents/information and an
Opportunity to submit them in a complete form.

pe It has been generally observed that the applications for exemption
remain pending in the offices for very long periods. Relaxation under para 79 of
the Scheme is meant only to avoid the difficulty of making an applicant
establishment comply as an unexempted establishment during the period its

exemption application is being processed and is pending a decision by the

§ gov 5 overent The said period is at best contemplated to be brief but
it has been found that relaxation is treated as defacto exemption by
the RPFCs as well as the employer and there is no effort to dispose of the
exemption application thereafter. This is not only incorrect but the pendency of

the applications for exemption for unduly long periods earns EPFO a bad name.

3: It has hence been decided that upon receipt, an exemption.

proposal be promptly examined within a week. All complete applications must be 3

forwarded to this office along with the RPFC's recommendations. In other cases,
the deficiencies/missing information/documents, if any, may be objectively listed
and the exemption application be returned to the employer requesting him to
submit the same in a complete state within a reasonable timeframe preferably 15
days. In case, the employer is not able to furnish the requirements a show
cause notice may at once be issued by: the RPFC calling upon the employer to
show cause as to why it may not be presumed that he has no intention of
submitting a complete exemption proposal and therefore why his establishment
should not be asked to comply as an unexempted establishment. In case the
employer, without a good and sufficient cause, fails to submit a complete
exemption proposal within the notice period the RPFC should proceed to secure
compliance as an unexempted establishment. It is hence always essential for
the RPFC to ensure that relaxation is granted subject to the condition that a
complete exemption application has been received.

4. In case, however, an establishment submits an incomplete
exemption proposal alongwith an explanation as to why it is unable to furnish
one or more of the essential standard requirements of a complete proposal, the
RPFC concerned must process and forward the proposal to this office alongwith
his appropriate comments/recommendations. ,

Sir,


Please refer to this office letter no. C-II/Misc./2/06/x/EZ/46390-46425dated
27th September 2006 wherein the impact of the amendment to Income Tax Rules
brought out by the Finance Act, 2006 was communicated to the field offices
alongwith specific directions to dispose of the applications for grant of exemption
pending with the Regions expeditiously. As this is an opportunity available to EPFO
to regulate all the hitherto excluded PF Trusts, it is imperative that the opportunity for
growth in extending service to all excluded Trust funds is seized and the field offices
handle the application for coverage and exemption with sensitivity and firm
commitment.

2.
The CBT in its 176th meting has approved progressive changes in processing
the grant of exemption so as to facilitate the field offices to expeditiously dispose of
the applications seeking exemption under Section 17 of the Act. The major changes
approved are:


i.
Simplification of model rules and conditions for grant of exemption.

ii.
Shift from the position of discouraging exemption to a positive stand of
encouraging exemption.
iii.
Thorough scrutiny of exemption proposals at field level. At Head Office
checks of defined critical points so as to avoid duplication of work and
consequent delay.

iv.
Accepting certification by Chartered Company Secretary, Actuary and
Chartered Accountant regarding the comparison of benefits.

v.
Time bound plan for processing of exemption proposals.

vi.
Regular compliance audit of the exempted establishments especially of the
fiduciary role of the trust.

vii.
Adoption of uniform format of reporting (including accounting standard,
methods of valuation etc.) by all exempted trusts countrywide.
viii.
Single window clearance system for grant of exemption to establishments
having ‘recognized’ provident funds.

ix.
Exemption from Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995 to establishments
running pension schemes with benefits equal to or better than that available
under the Central/State Government.


Modalities on implementing the decision of 2(iv) (vi) and (vii) will be communicated
separately. Rest of the decisions shall be implemented strictly following the
guidelines below:

3.
The Board has also approved the following changes in the procedure for
scrutinizing the applications.

”Considering the difficulty experienced by the majority of industrial houses
in furnishing written consent of employees spread across different
locations, the procedure for obtaining the consent of the employees stand
modified. The employer shall display a notice stating the intention of
obtaining exemption under section 17(1)A of the Act Para 27A of the
Scheme to establish an exempted PF trust and calling for objections within
30 days of posting such notice on the notice board in the Head office of
the establishment and its branches. In addition, notice should also be
posted on the website of the establishment and mail the notice to the email ID of all the employees if available. A certificate of confirmation for
having published the notice as well as posting it in the website and emailing to the employees, as the case may be shall be filed by the
establishment. If no objection is received from the majority of the
employees within the reasonable time of 30 days of publishing the notice,
the establishment and the Board of Trustees shall certify this position and
it will be recorded as deemed consent of the majority of the employees”.

4.
The conditions to be satisfied by the establishment seeking exemption has
been categorised into

(a) Essential conditions for grant of exemption.
(b) Conditions which are required to be satisfied after grant of exemption.

The essential conditions to be followed while processing the applications and
conditions which are required to be satisfied after grant of exemption shall be
scrutinized separately. The essential requirements for considering the proposals
are:
i.
Application for exemption duly signed by the employer and addressed
to the Appropriate Government.

ii.
Three copies of PF Trust Rules duly signed by all the trustees
indicating their status in the Trust.
iii.
Certificates of undertakings by the employer to abide by the Condition
No.22 and Condition No.23 of appendix ‘A’ to Para 27AA as per
prescribed proforma.

iv.
Comparison of benefits under the PF Trust Rules vis-à-vis the benefits
available under the EPF Scheme, 1952 in the prescribed proforma.
